Sensory Tri-View · the offenders you ruled on, before and now (16 November 2026)

One bullet per offender, numbered as in your rulings. Every picture is the True-Person view from the held shoulder camera, with the state you ruled on beside the scene as it stands now. Seconds are the video player's.

Each bullet says what you are seeing, what is new to pass off on, and what to check has not changed.

Stand-ins in every picture: the simulated mannequin and its motion (rung 3), the timeline's timings (rung 4), the room, the trees, the bushes, the lamps and the light (rung 5), and the scans at 1024 where the piece will use 2048. What lasts is the rule each bullet names.

Fixed, for your pass-off

Ten rulings and one fault I found while fixing them.

  • 1The remembered window: its sill and its side are whole
    The window from the bed, his eyes shut in the doze, player 31.3 s.
    What you are seeing
    The window as he remembers it while his eyes are shut. Left, the state you ruled on. Right, now.
    New, to pass off on
    The sill is one ledge and the window's side is one face. The pale grey ball in the window is the remembered sun (your ruling 5): it is in the last picture his eyes took, and before it was see-through and all but invisible here.
    Check it has not changed
    The wavy outline of the frame is the memory's ripple, as you passed it. The two bushes and the ridge through the window.
    Why it happened
    From the bed his eyes see the top of the sill and the side of the window almost edge-on, so the picture holds only a few rows of them, with gaps between the rows. The outside showed through the gaps as white wedges. The picture he sees with his eyes open closes such gaps with the thing's known shape. The remembered picture now does the same for flat-faced things.
    Lasting or stand-in
    The rule lasts. The window and the room are stand-ins.
  • 2The end of the east wall is one edge, and the tree's trunk is one line
    At the window with the model zoomed out, player 82.0 s.
    What you are seeing
    Top row: the far end of the room's east wall, before and now. Bottom row: the left tree's trunk, before and now. Both enlarged four times.
    New, to pass off on
    The wall ends in one straight edge. The trunk is one line with no dots beside it.
    Check it has not changed
    The crown above the trunk keeps its smooth outline. The ground and the black places his eyes cannot see are as before.
    Why it happened
    The wall: his eyes see it almost edge-on from the window, so each row of the picture covers a hand's breadth of wall and the rows end at different places. The wall's known shape is there to close that edge, but its pieces were turned away from the camera's side and were never drawn. They are now turned the way the picture's own surface is turned. The trunk: it is five pixels wide in what his eyes see. A round thing that thin has no outline apart from its body, and the pieces meant to draw its outline came out as a broken row of dots. A round thing under six pixels thick is now drawn by the picture alone.
    Lasting or stand-in
    Both rules last and name no thing. The wall and the tree are stand-ins.

    Lasting or stand-in

  • 5The remembered sun is a ball again
    His eyes shut in the sun, player 105.3 s. The sun enlarged four times.
    What you are seeing
    Left, the remembered sun in the state you ruled on. Middle and right, now, at two moments 1.3 s apart.
    New, to pass off on
    A grey ball, opaque as every memory is, with the ripple's soft light and dark across it. It shimmers as the bushes do and stays a ball. At four times enlargement its outline is lumpy and, at the moment in the middle panel, a crease crosses it: that is the ripple itself, the same that bends the bushes. The clip sent with this page shows it moving.
    Check it has not changed
    The bushes and trees still shimmer as you passed them. The one rule added here trims only the largest movements of the smallest bushes.
    Why it happened
    Two causes. First: with his eyes shut the remembered sky is drawn a hair nearer than the sky he sees, and the sun ball was left where it was, so the remembered sky cut through the ball and only a sliver of it showed. The ball now moves with the remembered picture. Second, you were right that the sun's shimmer was stronger: I measured it. The ripple's waves are four times wider than tall. A bush is low and wide, so the waves barely bend it. The sun is as tall as it is wide and smaller than a wave, so it was sheared by a quarter of its size, twice as much as a bush as wide.
    The rule added
    No remembered thing that the mind holds whole is bent by its ripple by more than 15% of its own size. It applies to every such thing. The big bushes were already under it.
    Lasting or stand-in
    Both rules last. The sun ball's size and the bushes are stand-ins.

Needs your word

One thing, left exactly as it was until you say.

  • 7The ground his eyes cannot see, behind a bush: should it look like memory?
    He thinks of the view and what his eyes cannot see fills in, player 88.0 s.
    What this is not
    It is not about memory filling in the scene when he thinks of it. That is intended and it stays.
    What it is
    It is about how the filled-in ground looks. Left, as it is: the ground behind each bush, which his eyes cannot see, comes in at full colour and brightness, exactly like the ground he is seeing beside it. You cannot tell which ground he sees and which he only thinks is there. At the same moment the back of each tree's crown, also unseen, comes in pale and grey, as a memory.
    Your second reading
    You asked whether the ground and the bush merely happen to look alike once the memory effect is applied. They do not: the memory effect is not applied to that ground at all. It is drawn as if it were seen.
    The change, shown on the right
    The filled-in ground takes memory's look, greyer and dimmer, as the crown's back already does. By your own words, the point is to show the difference between what he sees and what he thinks he sees.
    Your word
    Say yes and I switch it on: it is one switch, already built and shown here. Say no and it stays as on the left.

  • 12 and 14Withdrawn, and the three questions you were curious about
    14's three questions
    I had listed three unlike numbers as if they answered one question about his lids. They answer three. Which picture is the last one he saw? The last frame with his lids less than a tenth closed. When do his eyes count as shut? When the lids are fully closed. Do his eyes still take in the far view, so that far things go on resolving? While the lids are less than half closed. Three questions, three marks, nothing to fix.
